# .NET Version Upgrade

## Preferences
- **Flow Mode**: Automatic
- **Target Framework**: net10.0

## Source Control
- **Source Branch**: master
- **Working Branch**: upgrade-dotnet-10
- **Commit Strategy**: After Each Task
- **Branch Sync**: Auto (Merge)

## Upgrade Options
- **Upgrade Strategy**: Bottom-Up
- **Project Approach**: In-place
- **Package Management**: Per-Project (defer CPM to post-migration)
- **Unsupported API Handling**: Fix Inline
- **Windows Native APIs**: Windows Compatibility Pack
- **Assembly Binding Redirects**: Document and Review Before Removing

## Strategy
**Selected**: Bottom-Up
**Rationale**: 2 projects (`PcapEventBridge.csproj`, `CLEVIR_INCA_7_5.vbproj`) are in scope for .NET retargeting and form a 2-tier dependency graph crossing the .NET Framework → modern .NET boundary (net48 → net10.0/net10.0-windows); per the .NET Framework migration planning rules, any Framework solution with 2+ projects requires Bottom-Up (non-negotiable), since the framework gap gives each tier genuinely different upgrade mechanics (SDK-style conversion, WinForms/GDI+ resolution, and binding-redirect reconciliation apply only to the app tier).

### Execution Constraints
- Strict tier ordering: Tier 2 (`CLEVIR_INCA_7_5.vbproj`) cannot start until Tier 1 (`PcapEventBridge.csproj`) is retargeted and validated with a standalone build.
- SDK-style conversion and TFM retarget for `CLEVIR_INCA_7_5.vbproj` are separate tasks/builds — never combine the structural conversion with the TFM/API-surface change in one build-fix pass.
- Package updates, binding-redirect review, and obsolete-API cleanup for `CLEVIR_INCA_7_5.vbproj` happen only after its TFM retarget succeeds, since several of those items (package removals, redirect relevance) are downstream of the retarget outcome.
- Final validation must include a runtime smoke test of ETAS INCA COM interop calls, not just a build/metadata-level check.

## Key Decisions Log
- 2026-07-02: Target framework confirmed as **.NET 10** (LTS, support to Nov 2028) over .NET 8/9. .NET 8 and .NET 9 share the same EOL date (Nov 2026) per current lifecycle data, so .NET 10 gives the longest runway for equivalent migration effort. Confirmed after empirically validating that the ETAS INCA vendor interop assemblies (`IncaCOM.dll`/`incacom`, `RCI2dotNet.dll`, `Interop.Scripting.dll`, `Etas.Base.ComSupport.dll`) load successfully in a live modern .NET (.NET 9) host process — both the repo-vendored copies (`lib\Interop\`) and the actual installed INCA 7.5 SDK copies (`C:\Program Files\ETAS\INCA7.5\cebra`) matched byte-for-byte in version (20.7507.0.208 / assembly v20.0.0.0), so no drift risk. A full runtime smoke test (not just metadata load) is still recommended during execution as final confirmation.
- 2026-07-02: `NCOMdecoder/` was found committed as a broken git "gitlink" (embedded repo pointing at `OxfordTechnicalSolutions/NCOMdecoder.git`, commit `6bd95e9`) with no `.gitmodules` registration — would have produced an empty folder on fresh clones. User chose to flatten it into normal tracked files (matching the existing `lib\Interop` vendoring pattern) rather than set it up as a proper git submodule. IDE cache (`.vs/`) and build intermediates (`*.obj`) were excluded via an updated `NCOMdecoder/.gitignore`.
- 2026-07-02: Project file has a stale reference version for `incacom` (declared `Version=19.0.0.0` vs actual binary `20.0.0.0`) — flagged for cleanup during assessment/execution, not currently build-breaking.
- 2026-07-02: Assessment generated for `net10.0` (solution-wide). No security vulnerabilities/CVEs found in package scan. Of the 53,947 raw reported issues, ~98% (45,607 binary-incompatible + ~8,300 source-incompatible WinForms/GDI+ references) are mechanical designer-generated API references that resolve automatically once `CLEVIR_INCA_7_5.vbproj` is retargeted to `net10.0-windows` with WinForms enabled — not manual fixes. The "Windows Forms Legacy Controls" bucket (1,431 issues) is also mostly a miscategorization: it's tagging current-gen replacement controls already in use (`MenuStrip`, `DataGridView`/`DataGridViewCell`) rather than actually-removed legacy controls (`StatusBar`, `ToolBar`, classic `MainMenu`/`ContextMenu` had 0 real hits). Real, non-mechanical migration items identified: (1) dead Remoting-lease code in `GM_INCA_Comm.vb` (`InitializeLifetimeService`/`ILease` override — dev's own comment says "This function no longer used..."; `System.Runtime.Remoting` has no compat shim in modern .NET, so this must be deleted, not ported), (2) [SUPERSEDED — see 2026-07-03 entry] originally-scoped obsolete crypto API modernization in `EncryptDecrypt.vb`, (3) `System.Speech` usage in `VoiceRecognitionClass.vb` (113 refs) — a compatible modern `System.Speech` NuGet package exists targeting `net10.0-windows` (verified via `get_supported_package_version`, resolves to `11.0.0-preview.5.26302.115`), so this is a package-swap, not a rewrite, (4) 7 mandatory binding-redirect MSB3836 conflicts + 8 potential forced-downgrade redirects in `app.config` that must be reconciled (mostly stale redirects predating the `incacom`/Azure.Core package version bumps), (5) mandatory SDK-style project conversion for `CLEVIR_INCA_7_5.vbproj`, (6) 9 package upgrades recommended — mostly churn from packages pinned to `11.0.0-preview.4/5.*` that should move to `10.0.9` stable (matching net10.0), plus `Newtonsoft.Json 13.0.5-beta1` → `13.0.4` stable.
- 2026-07-03: **Task 07 scope changed from "modernize crypto APIs" to "remove encryption/decryption entirely"**, per explicit user decision. A task-tracking file edit outside the normal tool flow had altered task 07's description to request full crypto removal instead of the originally planned `RijndaelManaged`/`SHA512Managed` modernization; this was flagged to the user rather than silently executed. Before acting, research surfaced that the decrypt path is wired into more than the requesting user's local flash-drive files: `VehicleStatDashboard.vb`'s "Find and Decrypt" tool (`FindAndDecryptToolStripMenuItem_Click`) recursively scans shared network locations (`Q:\`, `Q:\HighContent\VehicleData`, `Q:\HighContent\RideData`, `Q:\LowContent\VehicleData`) for `.encrypt` files in subfolders dated back to 2019/2020 and bulk-decrypts+deletes them — i.e. a multi-year shared archive, not just per-machine state. This was surfaced explicitly via `ask_question`; **user confirmed proceeding with full removal now, explicitly accepting that the existing `.encrypt` archive on those network shares becomes permanently unreadable/is abandoned** (no bulk-decrypt-first migration requested).
  - Revised scope for `07-obsolete-crypto-cleanup`: delete `EncryptDecrypt.vb`'s crypto primitives (`CreateKey`, `CreateIv`, `EncryptOrDecryptFile`, `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`, `HandleEncryptFileName`, `HandleDecryptFileName`) entirely — no `Aes.Create()`/`SHA512.Create()` modernization, since the functionality itself is being removed, not upgraded.
  - `EncryptFilesInDirectory`/`TriggerEncryptAndCopy` (also in `EncryptDecrypt.vb`) drive the flash-drive file-transfer workflow (calls `Module1.vb`'s `CopyFileToDDrive`) — this transfer mechanism is a **distinct feature from encryption** and was not asked to be removed. Keep the directory-walk/copy-to-flash-drive behavior; just stop calling `Encrypt()` and copy the plaintext file directly. Decided (not left ambiguous): do **not** delete the local original file after copy for these previously-encrypted file types — this matches the existing precedent already in the same function for `.log` files, which are copied unencrypted today and are never deleted locally afterward.
  - Remove the now-dead decrypt UI entry points in `VehicleStatDashboard.vb`/`VehicleStatDashboard.Designer.vb`: `DecryptFileToolStripMenuItem`, `FindEncryptedFilesToolStripMenuItem` (parent menu), `FindAndDecryptToolStripMenuItem` (child) — their Click handlers and Designer wiring — since decrypt capability is fully removed and the archive is abandoned.
  - `GM_ResidentClient.vb`'s `HandleBackgroundEncryption()` (calls `EncryptFilesInDirectory` every 10s while `UsingFlashDrive`) stays, just no longer produces `.encrypt` output once the above change lands.
  - The `MarshalByRefObject` investigation item (separate, on `GM_INCA_CommClass`) is unaffected by this change and remains an investigation-only item.
  - This is a larger blast-radius change than originally scoped (multiple files including a WinForms Designer file); the task-worker sub-agent should assess at execution time whether it needs decomposition into sub-tasks (e.g., crypto-primitive removal vs. UI-entry-point removal) per its normal Phase 3 gate.
- 2026-07-03: Task 02 (`PcapEventBridge.csproj` retarget) completed — straightforward `net48` → `net10.0` swap, zero code changes needed (source only uses `System`/`SharpPcap`, no framework-sensitive APIs). Both packages (`SharpPcap 6.3.1`, `PacketDotNet 1.4.9-pre53`) confirmed already at their net10.0-compatible versions via `get_supported_package_version` — no bump required. No test project covers this library (solution has no test projects at all — confirmed via `discover_test_projects` across all 4 solution projects).

## Build Tool Decisions
- **PcapEventBridge.csproj**: `dotnet build` (SDK-style, net10.0-only after retarget, no .resx/XAML/WinForms designer resources/COM refs) — validated standalone, builds clean with 0 errors/0 warnings.
